blind_spots.blind_spot: Voyager's perception layer runs 'foundation vision models' for real-time 3D mapping and obstacle detection on a 5.2 lb airframe (Halley)
blind_spots.operator_reality: Foundation vision models are power- and compute-hungry; on a sub-6lb SWaP-C budget with no mention of thermal management, sustained inference during a long-duration ISR loiter (not just a fast dash) will throttle or drain batteries faster than advertised flight specs suggest.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Specs are framed around top speed (>200mph) and altitude (<25ft AGL) — dash performance, not sustained-endurance power budget under continuous AI inference.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Voyager delivers real-time perception via foundation vision models, providing obstacle detection and 3D mapping for proactive avoidance in dynamic environments.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Product is pitched as 'no comms required' autonomous decision-making with onboard 3D mapping and threat tracking, but nowhere mentions ATAK/TAK integration
blind_spots.operator_reality: If Voyager's outputs don't feed into the ATAK common operating picture units already carry, an operator gets a second disconnected display to manage mid-mission instead of one unified feed — exactly the kind of integration gap that kills adoption after the demo.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The site emphasizes standalone autonomy ('any platform, any mission') rather than integration into existing government C2/SA tooling.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Fusing AI-driven perception, navigation, and control into a compact module, it can be integrated on any platform and customized for your unique mission sets.

blind_spots.blind_spot: CMMC Level 2 certification was just announced (June 2026) with no visible compliance/ISSO hire on the jobs list
blind_spots.operator_reality: A cert without a dedicated owner tends to decay — POA&Ms go stale, new code paths ship without re-assessment, and the next contract's compliance review finds the same gaps the cert was supposed to close.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Open roles skew toward hardware/test/field (PCB, FPGA, UAS Test) with a generalist 'Head of IT' but nothing titled compliance, ISSO, or RMF.

opener_hook: Halley validated C-UAS and one-way-attack profiles at T-REX 26-2 in May — did the foundation-vision perception pipeline hold frame rate when the RF link degraded, or only when GPS did?
what_they_do: Builds Voyager, a hardware+software autonomy stack, and Halley, a VTOL drone, for GPS-denied navigation and autonomous target engagement in contested environments.
